Class ClientHandler

java.lang.Object
de.lmu.dbs.ifi.sep25.network.ClientHandler
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable
public class ClientHandler extends Object implements Runnable
The ClientHandler class is responsible for managing communication between the server and a specific connected client. Each instance of this class runs on its own thread and listens for incoming messages from the client, processes them, and sends responses or broadcasts as appropriate.

The class supports a range of message types, each of which is handled by a specific method. It ensures the integrity of communication by adhering to the server protocol and allows clients to perform operations such as sending messages, setting their status, and more.

This class is intended to be used within the context of a server that supports multiple connected clients and provides mechanisms for broadcasting messages, client lifecycle management, and error handling.

    • run

      public void run()
      Executes the main logic for handling incoming messages from a client. This method reads JSON-formatted messages from the client's input stream, determines the message type, and delegates processing to the appropriate handler method.

      The method operates as follows: - Reads JSON messages from the input stream using the `reader` object. - Parses each message to extract the `messageType` field. - Based on the `messageType`, forwards the message to specific handler methods (e.g., `handleBodyAlive`, `handleBodySendChat`, or `handleBodyReceivedChat`, among others).

      If an unrecognized message type is encountered, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException` with a description of the unknown type.

      The method runs continuously within a loop until the input stream is closed or an exception occurs. Any `IOException` during execution is caught and logged using `printStackTrace` for debugging purposes.

      This method is invoked automatically when the thread associated with the `ClientHandler` instance is executed.

      Specified by:
      run in interface Runnable

    • setReadyRegister

      public void setReadyRegister()
      Marks the entity associated with this instance as ready to register in the server and broadcasts a message indicating completion of the selection process.

      This method performs the following actions: 1. Marks the entity identified by `myID` as ready for registration using the server instance. 2. Broadcasts a message to notify other entities about the completion of the selection process for this instance.

      Utilizes the `server` instance for registration marking and the `broadcastMessage` method to send out a notification message.

    • checkLiveness

      public void checkLiveness()
      Validates the liveness state of the client connection and sends a "BodyAlive" message to the client to indicate activity. This method performs the following actions:

      - Sets the alive flag to false, potentially signaling that the client's connection or activity needs to be verified. - Sends a message containing a MessageDefinitions.BodyAlive object to the client. The message is serialized using the MessageDefinitions.Message wrapper and dispatched using the sendMessage(Message) method.

      This method may be used for periodic health checks to ensure that the client is responsive and able to receive and process messages properly.

    • sendMessage

      public void sendMessage(MessageDefinitions.Message<?> msg)
      Serializes a given MessageDefinitions.Message object to its JSON string representation and sends it to the client. The method uses a JSON library to perform serialization and delegates the actual transmission to the overloaded sendMessage(String) method.

      If serialization or transmission fails, the exception is caught and an error message is printed to the error output stream.

      Parameters:
      msg - the MessageDefinitions.Message object to be serialized and sent

    • closeAll

      public void closeAll()
      Closes all resources associated with the client connection managed by this ClientHandler. This includes removing the client handler from the server's management, closing the input/output streams, and terminating the socket connection, if applicable.

      This method performs the following actions:

      • Removes the current client handler instance from the server's client handler list.
      • Closes the input stream reader if it is not null.
      • Closes the output stream writer if it is not null.
      • Closes the socket connection if it is open and not already closed.
      • Sets the alive flag to false, marking the client handler as inactive.
      • Outputs a log statement indicating the connection closure.

      Any IOException that occurs during the resource cleanup process is caught and logged to the error stream. The connection cleanup process continues for other resources even if an exception occurs.
